intended_object: The Hopf-algebra map O(G_gen) → O(T) dual to the inclusion of the spin weight torus T = D(ℤ^{n+1}) into the subgroup G_gen ⊆ GL_{2^{n+1}} over R generated by the type-B_{n+1} spin root subgroups and the weight torus. In other words, the weight-torus homomorphism T → GL corestricted to G_gen. This is taken from the docstring, the module documentation and the companion theorem.
explanation:
In the library, the generated subgroup's coordinate Hopf algebra is the quotient of O(GL) by the common kernel Hopf ideal of the generator maps. Its generators are the root subgroups (indexed by `.inl`) and the weight torus (indexed by `.inr ()`). `generatedCoordinateLift` is the factorization of each generator's coordinate map through this quotient. Applying it at `.inr ()` therefore gives exactly the coordinate map of the torus generator, viewed as landing in the generated subgroup.

The theorem stated right after the definition confirms this. Precomposing with the quotient map `generatedCoordinateMap` recovers the ambient weight-torus map `weightTorusBaseChangeCoordinateMap ℤ R (basisWeight n)`. So the definition is the corestriction of the torus homomorphism T → GL to the generated subgroup G_gen, as the docstring says.

This is a specific morphism tied to the specific spin construction, so it is not too narrow. It is already stated over an arbitrary commutative ring R. Mathlib has no counterpart.
